modules.title: Introduction to Chemistry & Lab Safety
lessons: Why chemistry matters for engineers
Lab conduct, housekeeping and hygiene
Glassware, equipment and tools
Handling, storing and labelling chemicals
Personal protective equipment (PPE)
Waste disposal, first aid and spills
key_rules: Always add concentrated acid to water (AAA), never water to acid.
Wear splash goggles, buttoned full-length lab coat, chemical-resistant gloves, long pants, and closed-toe shoes.
Tie back long hair and remove dangling jewelry and synthetic fingernails before lab work.
Segregate acids, bases, organic solvents, heavy-metal inorganics, and neutral salts.

practice_questions.q: Which GHS pictogram shows a flame over a circle and warns that a chemical can intensify fires?
Why must sulfuric acid waste never be poured into a sodium hydroxide waste carboy?
options: Violent exothermic neutralization can boil and splatter corrosive liquid
It turns into an organic solvent
It lowers the pH to neutral without heat
practice_questions.answer: Violent exothermic neutralization can boil and splatter corrosive liquid

modules.title: Basic Chemical Concepts
lessons: Classifying matter
States, properties and changes of matter
Measurement and SI units
Significant figures and rounding
Scientific notation, accuracy and precision
Dimensional analysis
The mole and molar mass
key_rules: Elements contain one atom type; compounds have fixed ratios of chemically bonded atoms; mixtures are physically separable blends.
Multiply/divide: round to fewest sig figs. Add/subtract: round to fewest decimal places.
1 mol = 6.022e23 particles; M = n / V(L); C1*V1 = C2*V2.

practice_questions.q: How do you distinguish a compound from a mixture at the particle level?
options: A compound has different atoms chemically bonded in a fixed ratio; a mixture has unbonded substances blended together
A compound can be separated by filtration; a mixture cannot
A mixture has only one type of atom
practice_questions.answer: A compound has different atoms chemically bonded in a fixed ratio; a mixture has unbonded substances blended together

practice_questions.q: Calculate the product 4.20 cm × 2.1 cm using proper significant figures.

modules.title: Thermochemistry & Equilibrium
lessons: Systems, surroundings, state functions and the First Law
Heat transfer, pressure-volume work and calorimetry
Enthalpy, thermochemical equations and Hess's law
Bond energies and reaction enthalpy estimation
Dynamic chemical equilibrium, Q vs. K and Le Chatelier's principle
key_rules: deltaU = q + w; q > 0 when heat is absorbed, w = -P*deltaV (1 L·atm = 101.3 J; expansion w < 0, compression w > 0).
q = m*c*deltaT; in coffee-cup calorimetry, q_reaction = -q_solution.
Reversing a thermochemical equation changes the sign of deltaH; multiplying scales deltaH by the same factor.
deltaH ≈ sum(E_broken) - sum(E_formed); pure solids and liquids are omitted from equilibrium constant K.

practice_questions.q: A system absorbs 560 J of heat and does 150 J of work on the surroundings. What is ΔU?
A gas is compressed from 8.0 L to 3.5 L against 1.20 atm (1 L·atm = 101.3 J). How much work is done?
Given C + O2 -> CO2 (ΔH = -394 kJ) and CO + 0.5 O2 -> CO2 (ΔH = -283 kJ), what is ΔH for C + 0.5 O2 -> CO?
For an exothermic equilibrium reaction, what happens when temperature is increased?
options: Equilibrium shifts left toward reactants and K decreases
Equilibrium shifts right toward products and K increases
practice_questions.answer: Equilibrium shifts left toward reactants and K decreases

modules.title: Electrochemistry
lessons: Redox reactions and oxidation numbers
Balancing redox equations in acidic solution
Balancing redox equations in basic solution
Galvanic vs. electrolytic cells and salt bridges
Standard reduction potentials and cell voltage
Cell potential, Gibbs free energy and electrolysis
key_rules: OIL RIG: Oxidation Is Loss of electrons (at anode); Reduction Is Gain of electrons (at cathode).
E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode; never multiply E°red by stoichiometric coefficients.
deltaG° = -n * F * E°cell (F = 96,485 C/mol); positive E°cell means spontaneous forward reaction.

practice_questions.q: Given E°(Ag+/Ag) = +0.80 V and E°(Cu2+/Cu) = +0.34 V, what is E°cell for Cu + 2Ag+ -> Cu2+ + 2Ag?
In a galvanic cell, which way do anions in the salt bridge migrate?
options: Toward the anode compartment to balance positive ion buildup
practice_questions.answer: Toward the anode compartment to balance positive ion buildup
